Respondent/Respondent:
 State Of Kerala
 Represented By Public Prosecutor,
 High Court Of Kerala,
 Ernakulam, Pin - 682031.

Application praying that in the circumstances stated therein the
High Court be pleased to suspend the sentence and fine imposed by the
court below by impugned Judgment in Sessions Case No.418 of 2020 on the
file of the Fast Track Special Court, Pattambi, dated 20.07.2022 till the
disposal of the appeal.

This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application
and upon hearing the arguments of M/S.P.Mohamed Sabah, Libin Stanley,
Saipooja, Sadik Ismayil, R.Gayathri, M.Mahin Hamza, Alwin Joseph,
Advocates for the petitioner and of Public Prosecutor for the respondent

,
the court passed the following:
 P.T.O.
 C.S.Sudha, J.
 --------------------------------------------------------------
 Crl.M.Appl. No.1 of 2023
 in
 Crl. Appeal No.663 of 2023
 ---------------------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 9th day of January 2025
 Order
This is an application filed under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. seeking suspension of sentence of the
appellant/accused in S.C. No.418 of 2020 on the file of the Court of Session, Palakkad.

The accused
Ayoo

1

has been found guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 447, 363, 376AB and 376(2)(m) IPC and Section 3(b)(d) read with Section 4, Section 5(i)(m) read with Section 6 & Section 7 read with Section 8 of the PoCSO Act.
The applicant/accused has been sentenced to varying terms of imprisonment for the aforesaid offences.
The sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
Therefore, the maximum period of imprisonment that the applicant/accused will have to undergo is for a period of twenty years.

2. The learned counsel for the applicant/accused quite persuasively argued that the evidence on record is totally insufficient to find that it was the applicant/accused who had committed the offences.
PW1, the injured, has no prior acquaintance with the applicant/accused.
No TIP was conducted.
Therefore, the identity of the applicant/accused is highly doubtful.
It is also pointed out that this is a case of false implication because the applicant has a theft case registered against him.
Hence, the police have falsely implicated the accused in this case as they were not able to find the actual abuser.
It is also pointed out that the accused has been undergoing imprisonment for the last two and a half years and therefore his sentence may be suspended.
3. The application is opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor who submits that the applicant/accused has criminal antecedents and he is an accused in a theft case.

It is also pointed out that PW6 has corroborated the prosecution version regarding the identity of the accused and therefore this is not a case in which the identity of the accused has not been established and therefore no special circumstances have been made out to suspend the sentence.
4. Heard both sides.
5. PW1, the victim in this case was only 5 years and 7 months old at the time of the incident.
The prosecution case is that on 13/04/2019 at 20:30 hours, the accused, with the intention of abusing PW1, criminally trespassed into the courtyard of her house in the absence of her parents.
PW1 was taken to the back of her house and sexually abused.
The accused is also alleged to have threatened the victim from disclosing the event to others.
6. The argument of the applicant/accused regarding the identity of the accused was considered by the trial court and has concluded that the prosecution has succeeded in establishing the case.

Further, it is well settled that in considering an application for suspension of sentence, the appellate court is only to examine if there is such patent infirmity in the order of conviction that renders the order of conviction prima facie erroneous.

Where there is evidence that has been considered by the trial court, it is not open to a court considering an application under Section 389 to reassess and /
reanalyze the same evidence and take a different view, to suspend the execution of the sentence and release the convict on bail.
The arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant/appellant can be considered while the appeal is heard on merits.
This is not a case in which the discretion under Section 389(1) is required to be invoked.
Therefore, taking into account all these factors, and the gravity of the offence committed by the accused, I am not inclined to suspend the sentence as prayed for.
Hence, the application is dismissed.
